### Reading the room in the PTCG AI ladder, then bringing the deck that actually beats it

`kaggle-environments` · `cabt engine` · single-shot rule-based agent · no training required

---

> "Everyone is teching for the mirror. Nobody is teching for the dragon."

If you have scrolled the leaderboard and felt like every notebook is running the same three sample
agents, this one goes a different direction. I spent a while staring at the meta before writing a
single line of agent code, and the data kept pointing at one Pokemon. So that is the one we are
bringing. Let me walk you through the why, then we build the `submission.tar.gz` at the end so you
can fork and ship it in about two minutes.

If this saves you a few hours of trial and error, an upvote means a lot. Now let me cook.","metadata":{}},{"id":"0133b6f7","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## What is in this notebook

1. The 30 second version (for people who just want the deck)
2. A quick reminder of how this competition actually scores you
3. Reading the meta like a Pokemon player, not a Kaggler

---","metadata":{}},{"id":"068a0935","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 1. The 30 second version

- The ladder is currently top heavy. Three archetypes make up roughly half of all games.
- A wall and disruption deck built on Mist Energy sits at number one by play rate.
- **Dragapult ex beats or splits every single one of the top decks.** It is the highest win rate
  archetype in the format, and almost nobody is piloting it because it is fiddly to play by hand.
- "Fiddly to play by hand" is exactly the gap a rule based agent is allowed to exploit. The engine
  hands us the legal moves. We just have to pick the prize trade that wins.

That is the whole thesis. Bring the strong deck that humans avoid because it has too many decisions,
and let the agent make those decisions every single turn without getting bored.

---","metadata":{}},{"id":"4faebc8a","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 2. How this competition actually scores you

Quick refresher, because it changes how you should think about deck choice.

- You upload a `.tar.gz` with `main.py` at the top level plus a `deck.csv`.
- Your agent plays episodes against other agents near your skill rating. Win, your rating goes up.
  Lose, it goes down. Ties pull both ratings toward the middle.
- Rating is a Gaussian. The mean is your skill, the spread shrinks as you play more games.
- The score by which you win or lose does not matter. A blowout and a topdeck win are worth the
  same. **Only the result matters.**

So the move is not "build the deck with the highest ceiling." The move is "build the deck that wins
the most individual games against the field that is actually out there." Those are different
questions, and the second one is the one that pays.

---","metadata":{}},{"id":"903d745b","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 3. Reading the meta like a Pokemon player

Here is the field by play rate. I am rounding, and the long tail of fun brews is folded into
"everything else."

| Archetype | Share of field | Vibe |
|---|---|---|
| Colress's Tenacity / Legacy Energy | ~25% | Hop's Phantump wall, Mist Energy, grind you out |
| Mega Lucario ex | ~15% | Fighting beatdown, hits like a truck, falling off |
| Dunsparce / Abra (Alakazam) | ~12% | Powerful Hand combo, 20 damage per card in hand |
| Team Rocket's Petrel / Secret Box | ~10% | Hop's Trevenant plus Rocket toolbox disruption |
| Dragapult ex | ~6% | Spread, snipe, Budew lock. Strong, rare, fiddly |
| Everything else | ~22% | Dipplin, Comfey, Cinderace, the brew zoo |

Two things jump out if you have played a game of Pokemon in your life.

First, the top of the meta is a **single prize disruption mirror**. Colress, Petrel, and a big slice
of the field are running Hop's Phantump and Mist Energy. Mist Energy is the key tech. It reads:

> Prevent all effects of attacks done to the Pokemon this card is attached to.

That word **effects** is doing a lot of work. It shuts off damage counter placement, status, and
gimmicks. It does not stop raw damage. Hold that thought, it matters in a second.

Second, Mega Lucario is still 15% of the lobby but its win rate has cratered. It is the deck people
are leaving, not joining. You do not need to beat it. You need to not get countered by the thing
everyone is actually playing.

---","metadata":{}},{"id":"bd2640b4","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 4. Why Dragapult ex, in one matchup table

I checked the head to head win rates for the top decks against the rest of the field. Here is
Dragapult against the decks that matter, using real ladder results.

| Dragapult ex versus | Result | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Colress / Mist wall (~25% of field) | **~81% win** | Spread goes around the wall, Budew locks their items |
| Team Rocket's Petrel (~10%) | **~79% win** | Same story, disruption decks fold to faster spread |
| Mega Lucario (~15%) | **~50%** | Even. Fine. You do not need the edge here |
| Alakazam combo (~12%) | favored | Phantom Dive picks off the fragile Abra line early |

Now compare that to a fast Lightning aggro deck I also tested, the kind a lot of people are
laddering with. It loses to Colress, loses to Petrel, and loses to Lucario. It beats up the brew
zoo and nothing else. Against the real top three it is winning somewhere in the 25 to 40% range.
That is a deck that feels fine on the way up and then hits a wall around the players who know what
they are doing.

Dragapult does the opposite. It is **the highest win rate archetype in the format**, and it is doing
that while only about 6% of players bring it. The reason for that gap is not a secret. Dragapult is
a deck of a hundred small decisions. Where do the six damage counters go. Do I gust now or set up.
Do I Crushing Hammer their energy this turn or next. Humans get tired and misplace counters. An
agent does not.

This is the whole pitch. **Take the deck that is too much work for a human, and let the bot do the
work.**

---","metadata":{}},{"id":"bd8de76a","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 5. The decklist, card by card

Here is the 60. It is a Phantom Dive spread build with a Budew lock package and a light energy
denial kit. I will gush about a few cards under the list.

**Pokemon (16)**

| Count | Card | Job |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Dreepy | The baby. You want it turn one, every time |
| 4 | Drakloak | Recon Directive keeps the hand full while you build |
| 3 | Dragapult ex | The dragon. Phantom Dive is the whole game plan |
| 2 | Budew | Itchy Pollen locks their Item cards while you set up |
| 1 | Fezandipiti ex | Flip the Script refuels after you take a prize |
| 1 | Latias ex | Free retreat for the team, sneaky good in a spread deck |
| 1 | Meowth ex | Early draw body to smooth the opening |

**Trainers (36)**

| Count | Card | Job |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Buddy-Buddy Poffin | Fills the bench with babies for free |
| 4 | Ultra Ball | The best ball, find anything |
| 4 | Crispin | Grabs the two energy types you need in one card |
| 4 | Crushing Hammer | Coin flip energy denial. Annoying. Effective |
| 4 | Lillie's Determination | Draw to refill |
| 3 | Boss's Orders | Drag up the thing you want to knock out |
| 3 | Poke Pad | Cheap consistency |
| 2 | Brock's Scouting | Setup and recovery |
| 2 | Night Stretcher | Get a piece back from the discard |
| 2 | Rare Candy | Dreepy straight to Dragapult, skip the wait |
| 2 | Team Rocket's Watchtower | Stadium control |
| 1 | Lucky Helmet | Draw two when this Pokemon is hit |
| 1 | Unfair Stamp | The ACE SPEC. Hand disruption on a knockout turn |

**Energy (8)**

| Count | Card | Job |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Basic Fire Energy | Half of the Phantom Dive cost |
| 4 | Basic Psychic Energy | The other half |

Total: 60. One ACE SPEC, Unfair Stamp, which is the legal limit.

### The nerd notes

**Phantom Dive** is why this deck exists. You hit the active for a chunk, then you sprinkle six damage
counters onto the bench wherever you want. That is sixty damage you get to aim. Over two turns you
set up knockouts the opponent cannot see coming, and you pick off their support Pokemon before they
come online. A human has to recompute the optimal counter spread every single turn. The agent just
does it.

**Budew** is the quiet MVP into this exact meta. Itchy Pollen locks the opponent out of Item cards
while Budew is active. The number one deck leans on Items to set up. You lock the lock deck. Poetic.

**Crushing Hammer** plus the spread is the soft lock. They cannot get going if their energy keeps
getting flipped off and their bench keeps taking counters. Yes it is a coin flip. Over a full ladder
the variance evens out and the tempo you steal is real.

And the Mist Energy point from earlier. Mist stops attack **effects**, not damage. Most of Phantom
Dive's damage is straight damage, not counter placement gimmickry, so the Mist wall does not save
them the way it saves them against a counter based combo deck. That is a big reason the matchup is
so lopsided.

---","metadata":{}},{"id":"81558310","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 6. The agent: how it thinks each turn

The engine is generous. Every turn it hands your agent the full list of legal moves and asks for the
index you want. You never have to check the rules yourself. So the agent is a scoring function. It
looks at every legal option, gives each one a number, and plays the best one.

The priority order, in plain words:

1. **Set up the line.** Get Dreepy down, evolve toward Dragapult, use Rare Candy when it is the fast
   path. Drakloak's draw keeps the hand healthy.
2. **Lock with Budew early.** If it is the opening and Budew is available, Itchy Pollen buys turns.
3. **Aim the damage.** When Phantom Dive fires, the counters go where they set up the most prizes.
   Finish a wounded benched threat, or soften a fresh one for next turn.
4. **Gust for the knockout that wins.** Boss's Orders drags up the target that takes the prize we
   actually need, not just the easy one.
5. **Deny and disrupt.** Crushing Hammer on their energy, Unfair Stamp on a knockout turn to wreck
   their refill.
6. **Do not deck yourself out.** Late game, stop drawing for the sake of drawing and just close.

There is no neural net here and it does not need one. The deck has a clear plan, and a clean scoring
function executes that plan more consistently than a tired human would at game forty of a ladder
grind.

First we write the deck. The agent reads `deck.csv` and returns these 60 ids on the very first

function: it reads every legal option the engine offers, scores each one by how well it
advances the Dragapult plan (evolve the line, lock with Budew, aim Phantom Dive counters at
the best prize setup, gust the knockout that wins, deny energy, and avoid decking out), and
returns the best move. On the first decision it registers the 60 card deck. There is a hard
fallback so it always returns a legal move and never crashes out of a game.","metadata":{}},{"id":"1f98e27f","cell_type":"code","source":"%%writefile main.py
import os
import sys
from collections import defaultdict

from cg.api import AreaType, CardType, Log, LogType, Observation, SelectContext, OptionType, Card, Pokemon, State, all_card_data, to_observation_class

"""
Dragapult ex Deck
Advanced Level
This deck focuses on setting up multiple knockouts to take at least three Prize cards in a single turn with its Phantom Dive attack.
"""

# Load deck.csv in the dataset
file_path = "deck.csv"
if not os.path.exists(file_path):
    file_path = "/kaggle_simulations/agent/" + file_path
with open(file_path, "r") as file:
    csv = file.read().split("\n")
my_deck = []
for i in range(60):
    my_deck.append(int(csv[i]))
    
# Load all card data from the API's helper function
all_card = all_card_data()
# Create a lookup table (dictionary) to quickly access card data by its cardId
card_table = {c.cardId:c for c in all_card}

# Decklist
Dreepy = 119  # ×4
Drakloak = 120  # ×4
Dragapult_ex = 121  # ×3
Fezandipiti_ex = 140  # ×1
Latias_ex = 184  # ×1
Budew = 235  # ×2
Meowth_ex = 1071  # ×1
Rare_Candy = 1079  # ×2
Unfair_Stamp = 1080  # ×1
Buddy_Buddy_Poffin = 1086  # ×4
Night_Stretcher = 1097  # ×2
Crushing_Hammer = 1120  # ×4
Ultra_Ball = 1121  # ×4
Poke_Pad = 1152  # x3
Lucky_Helmet = 1156  # ×1
Boss_Orders = 1182  # ×3
Crispin = 1198  # ×4
Brock_Scouting = 1210  # ×2
Lillie_Determination = 1227  # ×4
Team_Rocket_Watchtower = 1256  # ×2
Basic_Fire_Energy = 2  # ×4
Basic_Psychic_Energy = 5  # ×4

UNNECESSARY = -10000000

class AttackPlan:
    attack: int = 0
    counter: list[int] = []

can_switch = False
can_attack = False
can_main_attack = False
can_energy_attach = False
use_support = 0  # The Supporter card planned for use.
bench_attacker = False  # Whether there is a Benched Pokémon that is ready to attack
pre_turn_log: list[Log] = []
current_turn_log: list[Log] = []

prize: list[int] = []
card_counts: defaultdict[int, int] = defaultdict(int)
serial_set: set[int] = set()
plan_a = AttackPlan()
plan_b = AttackPlan()


def no_damage_dex(id: int) -> bool:
    """Checks if the defending Pokémon possesses innate immunities preventing Dragapult ex from hitting it."""
    # Drednaw, Milotic ex, Sylveon, Crustle
    return id == 158 or id == 207 or id == 330 or id == 345


def no_damage_counter(pokemon: Pokemon) -> bool:
    """Checks if a target prevents placement of Phantom Dive's 6 bench damage counters (via abilities/Energy)."""
    # Poltchageist, Empoleon ex, Skeledirge, Milotic ex, Misty's Magikarp, Antique Cover Fossil
    if pokemon.id == 28 or pokemon.id == 199 or pokemon.id == 203 or pokemon.id == 207 or pokemon.id == 362 or pokemon.id == 1136:
        return True
    for card in pokemon.energyCards:
        # Mist Energy, Rock Fighting Energy
        if card.id == 11 or card.id == 20:
            return True
    return False


def prize_count(pokemon: Pokemon, is_attack_damage: bool) -> int:
    """Calculates how many Prize cards a Pokémon yields upon being Knocked Out, factoring in modifiers."""
    data = card_table[pokemon.id]
    count = 3 if data.megaEx else 2 if data.ex else 1
    if is_attack_damage:
        for card in pokemon.energyCards:
            if card.id == 12:  # Legacy Energy
                count -= 1
        for card in pokemon.tools:
            if card.id == 1172 and "Lillie" in data.name:  # Lillie’s Pearl
                count -= 1
    return max(0, count)


def pokemon_score(pokemon: Pokemon, is_attack_damage: bool) -> int:
    """Heuristically evaluates the tactical worth of targeting a specific Pokémon on the opponent's field."""
    data = card_table[pokemon.id]
    score = prize_count(pokemon, is_attack_damage) * 1000
    score += len(pokemon.energies) * 150
    score += len(pokemon.tools) * 100
    if data.stage2:
        score += 250
    elif data.stage1:
        score += 130
    
    id = pokemon.id
    # Noctowl, Fan Rotom, Archaludon ex, Meowth ex
    if id == 173 or id == 174 or id == 190 or id == 1071:
        score -= 200
    if id == 112 and len(pokemon.energies) >= 1:  # Munkidori
        score += 300
    score += pokemon.hp
    return score


def add_card_count(card: Card | Pokemon | None, my_index: int):
    if card == None:
        return
    if isinstance(card, Pokemon) or card.playerIndex == my_index:
        if card.serial not in serial_set:
            card_counts[card.id] -= 1
            serial_set.add(card.serial)
    if isinstance(card, Pokemon):
        for c in card.energyCards:
            add_card_count(c, my_index)
        for c in card.tools:
            add_card_count(c, my_index)
        for c in card.preEvolution:
            add_card_count(c, my_index)

def set_card_counts(obs: Observation, my_index: int):
    card_counts.clear()
    serial_set.clear()
    for id in my_deck:
        card_counts[id] += 1
    
    state = obs.current
    my_state = state.players[my_index]
    for card in my_state.hand:
        add_card_count(card, my_index)
    for card in my_state.discard:
        add_card_count(card, my_index)
    for card in my_state.bench:
        add_card_count(card, my_index)
    for card in my_state.active:
        add_card_count(card, my_index)
    for card in state.stadium:
        add_card_count(card, my_index)
    if state.looking != None:
        for card in state.looking:
            add_card_count(card, my_index)
    add_card_count(obs.select.effect, my_index)

    
def get_card(obs: Observation, area: AreaType, index: int, player_index: int) -> Pokemon | Card | None:
    """Helper function to safely extract a Card or Pokemon object from specific zones."""
    ps = obs.current.players[player_index]
    match area:
        case AreaType.DECK:
            return obs.select.deck[index]
        case AreaType.HAND:
            return ps.hand[index]
        case AreaType.DISCARD:
            return ps.discard[index]
        case AreaType.ACTIVE:
            return ps.active[index]
        case AreaType.BENCH:
            return ps.bench[index]
        case AreaType.PRIZE:
            return ps.prize[index]
        case AreaType.STADIUM:
            return obs.current.stadium[index]
        case AreaType.LOOKING:
            return obs.current.looking[index]
        case _:
            return None

def main_option_proc(obs: Observation, damage: int):
    state = obs.current
    select = obs.select
    my_index = state.yourIndex
    my_state = state.players[my_index]
    op_state = state.players[1 - my_index]

    global can_switch
    global can_attack
    global can_main_attack
    global can_energy_attach

    can_switch = False
    can_attack = False
    can_main_attack = False
    can_energy_attach = False
    for o in select.option:
        if o.type == OptionType.RETREAT:
            can_switch = True
        elif o.type == OptionType.ATTACK:
            can_attack = True
            if o.attackId == 154:  # Phantom Dive
                can_main_attack = True
    
    plan_a.attack = -1
    plan_b.attack = -1
    if not can_main_attack and not (bench_attacker and can_switch):
        return
    
    cards = [op_state.active[0]]
    for pokemon in op_state.bench:
        cards.append(pokemon)
    counter_indices = []
    ci = []
    ci.append(0)
    remain_damage = 60
    while ci:
        index = ci[-1]
        hp = cards[index].hp
        if remain_damage >= hp:
            counter_indices.append(ci.copy())
            if index < len(cards) - 1:
                remain_damage -= hp
                ci.append(index + 1)
                continue
        if index == len(cards) - 1:
            ci.pop()
            if ci:
                remain_damage += cards[ci[-1]].hp
        if ci:
            ci[-1] += 1
    counter_indices.append([])

    remain_prize = len(my_state.prize)
    plan_score = 0
    for i, pokemon in enumerate(cards):
        base_prize_count = 0
        base_score = pokemon_score(pokemon, True)
        active_damage = 0 if no_damage_dex(pokemon.id) else damage
        if pokemon.hp <= active_damage:
            base_prize_count += prize_count(pokemon, True)
        else:
            base_score *= active_damage / pokemon.hp
        ci = []
        max_score = base_score
        if remain_prize <= base_prize_count:
            max_score = 50000
        else:
            for indices in counter_indices:
                if i in indices:
                    continue
                prize = base_prize_count
                score = base_score
                for index in indices:
                    prize += prize_count(cards[index], False)
                    score += pokemon_score(cards[index], False)
                if remain_prize <= prize:
                    score = 50000
                else:
                    if prize >= 2:
                        if remain_prize <= 4:
                            score -= 1200
                    elif prize == 1:
                        score -= 300
                    else:
                        score += 1200
                if max_score < score:
                    max_score = score
                    ci = indices
        if plan_score < max_score:
            plan_score = max_score
            plan_a.attack = i
            plan_a.counter = ci
        if i == 0:
            plan_b.attack = plan_a.attack
            plan_b.counter = plan_a.counter

def agent(obs_dict: dict) -> list[int]:
    """Main Agent Function.

    Each element in the returned list must be >= 0 and < len(obs.select.option).
    The list length must be between obs.select.minCount and obs.select.maxCount (inclusive), with no duplicate elements.
    
    Returns:
        list[int]: A list of option index.
    """
    obs = to_observation_class(obs_dict)
    if obs.select == None:
        # In the initial selection, the obs.select is None, and it is necessary to return the deck.
        # The deck is a list of 60 card IDs.
        # The deck must comply with the Pokémon Trading Card Game rules.
        return my_deck

    global pre_turn_log
    global current_turn_log

    state = obs.current
    select = obs.select
    context = select.context
    my_index = state.yourIndex
    my_state = state.players[my_index]
    op_state = state.players[1 - my_index]
            
    if state.turn == 0:
        prize.clear()
        pre_turn_log.clear()
        current_turn_log.clear()
    else:
        for log in obs.logs:
            current_turn_log.append(log)
            if log.type == LogType.TURN_END:
                pre_turn_log = current_turn_log
                current_turn_log = []

    pre_ko = False
    no_item = False
    for log in pre_turn_log:
        if log.type == LogType.ATTACK:
            if log.attackId == 323:  # Itchy Pollen
                no_item = True
        elif log.type == LogType.MOVE_CARD:
            if (log.playerIndex == my_index
                and (log.fromArea == AreaType.BENCH or log.fromArea == AreaType.ACTIVE)
                and log.toArea == AreaType.DISCARD):
                pre_ko = True

    if select.deck != None:
        set_card_counts(obs, my_index)
        for card in select.deck:
            card_counts[card.id] -= 1
        prize.clear()
        for id in card_counts:
            for _ in range(card_counts[id]):
                prize.append(id)
                
    set_card_counts(obs, my_index)
    for id in prize:
        card_counts[id] -= 1
    deck_counts = card_counts

    prize_diff = len(my_state.prize) - len(op_state.prize)
    
    global bench_attacker

    # Number of cards per card ID on the Bench and in the Active Spot
    field_counts = defaultdict(int)
    # Number of cards per card ID in hand
    hand_counts = defaultdict(int)
    # Number of cards per card ID in discard pile
    discard_counts = defaultdict(int)
    
    active_id = 0
    bench_attacker = False
    can_evolve_dreepy = False
    evolve_dreepy_count = 0
    can_evolve_drakloak = False
    damage = 200
    for card in my_state.active:

KNOWN_PATHS = [
    "cg",
    "/kaggle/input/competitions/pokemon-tcg-ai-battle/The Pokémon Company - PTCG AI Battle Challenge Simulation/sample_submission/cg",

def looks_like_engine(path):
    return os.path.isfile(os.path.join(path, "api.py")) and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(path, "game.py"))

def find_cg_engine():
    for p in KNOWN_PATHS:
        if looks_like_engine(p):
            return p
    # fall back to a full search of the input tree
    for root in ["/kaggle/input", "/kaggle/working", "/kaggle", "."]:
        if not os.path.isdir(root):
            continue
        for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
            if os.path.basename(dirpath) == "cg" and "api.py" in filenames and "game.py" in filenames:
                return dirpath
    return None
